title: QBR Decision Studio playbook and practical rehearsal notes
content:
Purpose: A compact "Decision Studio" playbook for high-signal QBRs focused on making 1–2 concrete renewal decisions per session. This doc is intended for CS Leads and AEs running QBRs for mid-market and strategic accounts. It prioritizes rehearsal-ready scripts, a low-friction interactive agenda, and a preflight checklist so meetings actually land decisions and next steps.

Key principles (why this differs):
- Decision-first: every segment maps to an explicit decision or de-risking outcome rather than vague updates.
- 45–75 minute format: tuned for busy exec schedules while preserving enough time for alignment.
- Rehearsal friction reduced: micro-scripts, timing cues, and a compact materials list so reps can practice in 15 minutes.

Outcome options (pick 1–2 per QBR):
- Renewal commitment (verbal + next-step PO/contract touch)
- Scope change approval (new feature / pilot OK)
- Escalation accepted (SOW or tech remediation timeline)
- Pause/monitor (extend evaluation window with measurement plan)

Who to invite and roles (minimum invite set):
- CS Lead (facilitator / decision owner)
- Account Executive (commercial lead)
- Product/PM (subject matter expert) — optional for feature asks
- Engineering lead / Solutions Engineer (technical risks + mitigation) — optional if demo or infra changes expected
- Customer sponsor + 1–2 senior stakeholders (decision authority)
- Note-taker (record decisions and owners)

Prework (sent 5 business days before):
- One-page 3-up: current usage/health, key risks (top 3), and suggested decisions. (attach as pre-read)
- Ticket digest: open tickets > P2 in past 90 days for this account (one slide).
- Renewal health snapshot: ARR, usage trend, adoption signal index (simple table).
- Ask stakeholders to pre-rank top 3 priorities (quick form).

Meeting agenda (60 minutes — adjustable):
1) 0:00–0:05 Opening & alignment (CS Lead)
   - Micro-script: "Thanks for time — goal today is to align on X and leave with a clear next step on Y. We’ll surface risks and close with a decision and owners."
   - Confirm who’s on the call and decision roles.
2) 0:05–0:15 Health snapshot & signal walk (CS Lead + Note-taker visuals)
   - Show 3-slide pre-read: Usage, adoption signals, and top risks.
   - Ask: "Do these signals match your perspective? Anything missing?" (clock 2 minutes for fast reactions)
3) 0:15–0:30 Priority Thermometer exercise (interactive)
   - Facilitated poll: stakeholders rank top 3 priorities (live or pre-submitted).
   - Map priorities to potential decisions on screen (Decision A/B/C).
   - Micro-script to nudge: "If we prioritize A, here’s the expected impact on X and the cost on Y."
4) 0:30–0:45 Deep-dive on 1 selected decision (SE/Eng/Product as needed)
   - Tech readout limited to 7 minutes (concise ask, risk, mitigation, timeline).
   - Demo guidance: 60–90s clip or short recording preferred; no ad-hoc long demos.
   - Decision framing: options, tradeoffs, required commitment (who signs/what date).
5) 0:45–0:55 Decision capture & owner alignment (AE + CS Lead)
   - Read back the chosen option, clarify acceptance criteria and success metrics.
   - Assign owners and deadlines. Use the Decision Card template (see below).
6) 0:55–1:00 Close & next steps (CS Lead)
   - Confirm follow-ups, required artifacts, and next check-in cadence.

Facilitation scripts (rehearsal-ready snippets):
- Kickoff (30s): "Hello everyone — to respect your time, I’ll keep the overview crisp and we’ll focus on the single decision that most affects renewal. By the end we’ll have a named owner and a next-step date."
- Surface disagreement (20–40s): "I hear differences — can we capture the two perspectives and quickly agree which risk we must mitigate by [date]? If not, we’ll escalate to X by [date]."
- Pause a derailing long-form debate (20s): "Great point — to preserve everyone’s time, can the team who wants deeper technical discussion take an action to produce a 10-minute readout by [date]? For this meeting, let’s decide on the tradeoff."
- Closing ask for commitment (25s): "Do we have the agreement to proceed with [option]? If yes, who will be the owner and when will the first milestone be delivered?"

Interactive activities (templates and how-to):
- Priority Thermometer (5–10 min): Visual slide with top 6 priorities; stakeholders drop 3 votes; facilitator normalizes to top 2. Outcome: maps to 1–2 candidate decisions.
- Signal-to-Impact mapping (10 min): For each top risk, map expected revenue/usage impact and mitigation cost; annotate with confidence bands.
- Decision Card (one-liner capture): Decision title | Chosen option | Owner | Success metric | First milestone (date) | Escalation point (if not met).

Decision Card example (copy to meeting notes):
- Decision title: Move to pilot X with 100 seats
- Chosen option: 3-month paid pilot, 100-seat uplift
- Owner: AE – Jordan Patel; CS owner: Avery Chen
- Success metric: 30% seat activation within 45 days
- First milestone: Contract addendum signed by 2026-01-15
- Escalation: If activation < 15% by day 30, schedule SRE + SE session within 7 days

Preflight checklist (run 30–60 minutes before):
- Calendar & dial-in check: correct invite roles and decision-makers on the event
- Pre-reads uploaded to meeting doc and linked in chat
- Dashboard links validated and short reproducible snapshot taken
- Demo artifacts queued (recording or 60s clip) and SE on standby
- Note-taker assigned and Decision Card prepared as a comment template
- Recording permissions confirmed and chat moderation assigned

Common escalation lanes (quick reference):
- Tech showstopper (blocker preventing go/no-go): escalate to SRE + Solutions Eng. Target response: 48 hours for triage, 5 business days for remediation plan.
- Commercial blocker (pricing/contract disputes): AE to propose 2 options within 3 business days; CSM to schedule negotiator touch.
- Adoption risk (usage drop > 20% month-over-month): CS + PM to run a 14-day activation blitz with defined measure windows.

Practice & rehearsal guidance (15-min kit for reps):
- 10 min: run verbal walkthrough with peer (use the micro-scripts above).
- 5 min: read Decision Card + confirm owner names and dates.
- Optional: record a 3-minute dry run for manager feedback.

Notes on measurement and follow-up:
- Record each Decision Card into the account’s renewal tracker (sheet id in linked_artifacts).
- Tag follow-ups in Jira (example JIRA-CS-xxxx). Update status weekly.

Email & calendar copy snippets (short):
- Calendar subject: "QBR: 45m Decision Studio — [Account] — Goal: Decide [X]"
- Pre-read note (one-liner): "Attached: 3-slide health + suggested decisions. Please quickly rank your top 3 priorities before the meeting so we can surface the right decision."
- Post-meeting decision note: "Decision made: [one-line]. Owner: [name]. Deliverable: [milestone] by [date]. If you disagree, reply within 48 hours or we’ll proceed."

Common failure modes and mitigations: 
- Failure: No decision because data absent. Mitigation: Annex short data ask to the calendar invite and mark decision as "deferred" with a 7-day data delivery SLA.
- Failure: Too many attendees talking. Mitigation: Run the Priority Thermometer asynchronously before the meeting and shorten live discussion to 10 minutes.
- Failure: Demo runs long and derails timebox. Mitigation: use 60s recorded demo or a 7-minute tech readout; book separate deep-dive.

Appendix: Short templates (copyable)
- Decision Card (single line): "[Decision title] — [Chosen option] — Owner: [name] — Milestone: [date] — Metric: [KR]"
- Quick poll question (Slack/MS form): "Rank these 6 priorities for next 90 days. Drag top 3."

Next steps for this draft:
- Gather feedback from 3 CS Leads after running 2 Decision Studio QBRs (target: Dec 2025).
- Convert Decision Card into a JIRA template and wire into account renewal board.

Document history: created by Avery Chen, 2025-11-06. Draft rehearsal notes updated 2025-12-02 after two internal dry runs.
